title: Self-Equivalence Groups of Permuted Modular Addition
summary: Exact counts are known for word sizes 3–5, with matching lower bounds through 64; prove or refute that the same counts are exact for every word size at least 3.

formal_statement.body: For permuted modular addition with word size $n$, prove or refute the conjecture that, for every integer $n \ge 3$, its full affine self-equivalence group has cardinality $3\cdot 2^{2n+8}$ and its full linear self-equivalence group has cardinality $3\cdot 2^{2n+2}$. These formulas give the exact cardinalities for $n\in\{3,4,5\}$; for $6\le n\le 64$, self-equivalences attaining these cardinalities are known only as lower bounds on the full groups.

scope.domain: Algebraic structure of affine and linear self-equivalences of permuted modular addition.
assumptions: n is an integer at least 3.
parameters: n: word size of permuted modular addition
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute that the conjectured counts are the exact cardinalities of the full affine and linear self-equivalence groups for every integer n at least 3.
